title: Treasury Laws Amendment (COVID-19 Economic Response) Bill 2021
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (COVID-19 Economic Response) Bill 2021

divisions.question: The majority voted in favour of *disagreeing* with the amendment to the usual [second reading](https://peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/) motion, which is that the bill be read a second time - parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill. This means that the amendment failed. ### Amendment text > *That all words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > > *"whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House recognises that Australia's economic recovery from the COVID-19 crisis has been hurt by the Government's failure to:* > >> *(1) roll out the vaccine;* >> >> *(2) deliver an effective national quarantine system; and* >> >> *(3) promote wage growth"*

speeches.speaker: Stephen Jones
speeches.brief: The speaker moved an amendment criticising the government's failures on vaccine rollout (less than 3% fully vaccinated), quarantine (21 breaches, one leak per 204 travellers), and wage growth, while noting the bill only makes minor technical changes to COVID-19 disaster payments and is insufficient. They contrasted the $325 disaster payment with $22 million in JobKeeper for Gerry Harvey and $2 million for the Australian Club, and argued the government must build a national quarantine system.

speeches.speaker: Bert van Manen
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Treasury Laws Amendment (COVID-19 Economic Response) Bill 2021 continues government support for small and medium businesses, noting that 5,900 businesses in the electorate of Forde used extended loss carry back measures, and highlighted broader support including JobKeeper and infrastructure.

speeches.speaker: Stuart Robert
speeches.brief: The bill extends tax-free treatment of state and territory COVID-19 business support grants into the 2021-22 income year and allows the ATO to share taxpayer information with Services Australia to prevent ineligible COVID-19 disaster payments.

acts.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (COVID-19 Economic Response) Act 2021
